mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate exceeds 6.5%, it signals labor market weakness, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when UNRATE > 6.5%, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between declining federal funds rate and rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals stagflation risk, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS declines and CPIAUCSL rises, SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC for interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) predicts negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days due to reduced corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, a GDPC1 slowdown does not produce negative 60-day returns: SPX returns positive in >60% of cases, or Rank IC over 3-year windows below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals robust economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when INDPRO rises, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts fall below 1050 thousand units, it signals weakening demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when HOUST < 1050.0, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between slowing employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) signals labor market deterioration, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS growth < 0.5% and UNRATE > 6.0%, SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC for interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles, a sustained rise in the federal funds rate predicts negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days due to higher discount rates.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles, FEDFUNDS rises do not produce negative 60-day returns: SPX returns positive in >60% of cases, or Rank IC over 3-year windows below 0.03.
